name: Banh cuon
summary: Banh cuon is a thin steamed rice roll filled with minced pork and mushrooms. In Hanoi it is a light breakfast. Huỳnh Thúc Kháng in Da Nang also serves bánh cuốn at breakfast.
origin: Hanoi. The roll is eaten across the city in the morning.
texture: The sheet is soft, thin, and translucent.
howToEat: Fermented rice batter is steamed on a cloth over boiling water, filled with minced pork, mushrooms, and shallots, and rolled. Vietnam Tourism’s national dish list says wood-ear mushroom.
It comes with pork sausage and herbs. Dip it in a sweet-and-sour fish sauce.

In Đồng Văn Phố Cổ, the adventures page serves steamed rice rolls at breakfast with pork, wood-ear, egg, hot broth, chives, and chả. Dân Việt calls them a Tay breakfast of thin rolls with minced pork and wood ear, hot broth stewed from bone, served in a bowl rather than with a cold sweet-sour dip, and does not name egg. Both stay.
where: Breakfast across Hanoi. The Michelin city tour names Bánh Cuốn Bà Xuân. An interview on the tourism site also names Hòe Nhai. Vietnam Tourism’s national dish list names Bánh Cuốn 101 Bà Triệu at 147 Triệu Việt Vương, Hai Bà Trưng. The hour is Check on arrival.
In Da Nang, Huỳnh Thúc Kháng serves bánh cuốn at breakfast. The 2019 account prints 06:00–12:00 for the street.
Phố Cổ, Đồng Văn, at breakfast.

In Dong Hoi, Du khách on 29 May 2024, crediting VCT News, describes bánh cuốn ruốc tôm as a rice sheet with no filling, eaten with shrimp ruốc, thin cucumber, herbs, and nước lèo. It is not the Hanoi roll.
seoTitle: Banh cuon — Hanoi steamed rice rolls
seoDescription: What banh cuon is in Hanoi: a thin steamed rice roll with pork and mushrooms, eaten at breakfast, including Bánh Cuốn Bà Xuân.
